correctness.rationale: Barycentric point on facet i has E[r_j r_k]=(1+1_{j=k})/[d(d+1)] for j,k!=i and zero otherwise (Dirichlet(1,..,1)). For m=d+1, c=1/[dm], B=sum_i t_i A_i/c=T(I+11^T)-t1^T-1t^T. It acts as T on the common orthogonal complement of 1,t, and direct rank-two determinant gives det(sum t_i A_i)=c^m m T^(m-2)(T²-sum t_i²). The squarefree coefficient [prod t_i] is E(det R_strat)^2=C_d=m!/[m^(m-1)d^m]. For iid mixture A_pi, E det(R)^2=m! det(A_pi)=C_d(1-sum pi_i²). Cauchy-Schwarz yields unique uniform pi maximizer. Independent direct two-permutation rational second-moment checks: 12 cases, d=2,3,4 stratified + iid, including degenerate pi. Finite checks corroborate analytic rank-two proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Rademacher covariance-det lemma covers general iid samples and mathematically dominates that SUBCLAIM (not a new iid general theorem). It does not on its face yield the nonidentical independent stratified coefficient without the mixed evaluation. Reitzner–Schütt–Werner handle asymptotic simple-polytope boundary sampling, not a finite m-point one-per-facet design.

Exact second moments and a strict sharp design advantage are nontrivial, shape-invariant benchmarks for high-dimensional inscribed simplex sampling; the iid covariance identity is classical and is not claimed itself to be new.
